anchor: How sweet the answer Echo makes
note: In Greek myth Echo was a mountain nymph who could only repeat the last words spoken to her. Moore makes her the voice that answers music at night.

anchor: To Music at night
note: Music is capitalized as if it were a person, answered by Echo.

anchor: When, roused by lute or horn, she wakes
note: Lute: an old stringed instrument with a pear-shaped body, played by plucking.

anchor: And far away o’er lawns and lakes
note: Lawns: stretches of open grassland, here part of the night landscape.

anchor: Yet Love hath echoes truer far
note: Hath: has. Love’s echo is the answering sigh of the beloved.

anchor: Of horn or lute or soft guitar
note: The three instruments whose songs are repeated by echoes.

anchor: ’Tis when the sigh,—in youth sincere
note: Sincere: honest, meant in earnest.

anchor: The sigh that’s breathed for one to hear
note: The only true echo is when the loved one breathes the sigh back.

anchor: At the mid hour of night, when stars are weeping
note: The stars are pictured as weeping, perhaps as dew falls in the night.

anchor: To the lone vale we loved
note: Vale: a valley. Lone: solitary.

anchor: To revisit past scenes of delight
note: Revisit: to visit again. The speaker hopes a spirit might.

anchor: Then I sing the wild song it once was rapture to hear
note: Rapture: a state of great joy.

anchor: When our voices, commingling, breathed like one on the ear
note: Commingling: blending together. Their two voices once sounded as one.

anchor: my sad orison rolls
note: Orison: a prayer, a spoken plea to God.

anchor: When he who adores thee has left but the name
note: Adores: loves deeply, worships. The speaker is the one who adores his country.

anchor: Of a life that for thee was resign’d
note: Resign’d: given up. The speaker has given his life for his country.

anchor: Thy tears shall efface their decree
note: Efface: to rub out, to wipe away.

anchor: Every thought of my reason was thine
note: Reason: his thinking mind. All of it was devoted to the beloved.

anchor: Is the pride of thus dying for thee
note: The title’s Latin, pro patria mori, means “to die for one’s country.” The beloved “thee” is the country.

anchor: As slow our ship her foamy track
note: Track: the path of foam that a ship leaves behind it.

anchor: Against the wind was cleaving
note: Cleaving: cutting through. The ship cuts into the headwind.

anchor: Her trembling pennant still look’d back
note: Pennant: a long, narrow flag flown on a ship.

anchor: So loth we part from all we love
note: Loth: unwilling, reluctant, not wanting to do it.

anchor: When, round the bowl, of vanish’d years
note: The bowl is a drinking bowl, around which friends gather to talk of the past.

anchor: Each early tie that twined us
note: Tie: a bond, here of friendship or love. Twined: wound together.

anchor: Where all looks flowery wild and sweet
note: Flowery: full of flowers. Travelers find lovely scenes abroad.

anchor: If Heaven had but assign’d us
note: Assign’d: allotted by fate. Heaven might have given them a home there.

anchor: As travellers oft look back at eve
note: Oft: often. Eve: evening. Travelers look back at the fading light.

anchor: To gloom hath near consign’d us
note: Consign’d: handed over, here to sadness.

anchor: Oft, in the stilly night
note: Stilly: quiet and still, without a sound.

anchor: Ere slumber’s chain has bound me, Fond Memory
note: Ere: before. Slumber: sleep. Both are old poetic words.

anchor: Like leaves in wintry weather
note: The friends have fallen away as leaves drop in winter.

anchor: Some banquet-hall deserted
note: Banquet-hall: a large hall for feasts, here now empty.

anchor: Whose garlands dead
note: Garlands: wreaths of flowers hung for a feast. They are now withered.
